title: No music for the instrument; owing a debt to the drummers
summary: There was little music for xylophone except a George Hamilton Green book; he later helps other players because of what the drummers did for him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: So, I noticed that I could do what I wanted to do on those -- I found that not having any music -- there was no music for that instrument in those days, I had to on -- play like violin books, I'd learned to read out of
violin books --
Oh, really?
Yeah. There was no music written for it as such.
YEAH.
Except that George Hamilton Green had a book out, which was very good --
Yeah.
And most of the guys -- drummers the pit had that.
Yeah.

So, and a lot of them through experience would have-- that's why as I got older and I lived in California or even New York before I went in the early '40's, when guys would come to me and they wanted to ask me about different things about the instrument, the playing this way or how I used four hammers --
Yeah?
-- and the method I did with the different stroke, of using -- I felt that I owed it to somebody --
Yeah.
I felt I owed --
Yeah.
-- somebody what all those drummers and people had --
Had done for you?
-- had tried to do to help me.
Especially since there wasn't -- it wasn't -- there wasn't anything available to people.

No, there was nothing, and yet all during that time I was practicing scales and all that sort of thing at the theater, between theaters, then I'd come and do my act, I used to do -- they'd let me do one number that was a jazz type of number, where I could improvise on it.
Yeah.
And the guys in the pit said, 'Hey, that sounds good, that number you do.' And they would encourage you -- -- me.
Yes, yes.
-- So you'd get that little bit at a time -- little bit of time you're encouraged --
Right.
-- and think maybe yes. Now when I was working for Paul Ashlon, this is the way I met Victor Young, he was a violin player at the Uptown Theater, when I moved from the Oriental to the Uptown.
